```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
rd <- tools::parse_Rd(file.path("man", "CAs-package.Rd"))
license <- packageDescription("CAs", fields="License")
version <- packageDescription("CAs", fields="Version")
rd_html <- capture.output(tools::Rd2HTML(rd))
library(CAs)
require(prepplot)

## Note:  These functions are internal to the tools package, but are not exposed
##    and are therefore not intended to be used and are subject to change.
##    for that reason, they are replicated here to ensure they stay consistent
##    with this document

## based on tools:::RdTags
rd_get_tags <- function(Rd)
{
  res <- lapply(Rd, attr, "Rd_tag")
  if (length(res)) 
      simplify2array(res, FALSE)
  else character()
}

## based on tools:::.Rd_get_metadata
rd_get_metadata <- function(x, tag)
{
  x <- x[rd_get_tags(x) == sprintf("\\%s", tag)]
  if (!length(x)) 
      character()
  else unique(trimws(vapply(x, paste, "", collapse = "\n")))
}

## might also want to capture html output for markdown.  This is more fragile
rd_html_get <- function(rd_html, from_h3, to_h3)
{
  #from_h3 <- "Details"
  #to_h3 <- "Author"
  ind_from <- grep(paste0("<h3>", from_h3), rd_html)
  ind_to <- grep(paste0("<h3>", to_h3), rd_html)
  if (length(ind_from) != 1 | length(ind_to) != 1 | all(ind_from == ind_to))
  {
    stop("from_h3 or to_h3 are not specified correctly")
  }
  return(rd_html[(ind_from + 1):(ind_to - 1)])
}

my_Rd_expr_doi <- function (x) 
{
    x <- tools:::.canonicalize_doi(x)
    sprintf("[doi: %s](https://doi.org/%s)", x, x)
}
```

## Warning
This is an early version of R package **CAs**. Some functionality is more mature than others. Especially the functionality on sequence covering arrays is still experimental, and changes that break backwards compatibility are not unlikely to occur.\cr
Important changes/bug fixes are stated in the [NEWS](https://github.com/ugroempi/CAs/blob/main/inst/NEWS.md) file.\cr
As stated in the [GPL-3 license](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.en.html), the package comes without any warranty.

## Installation
**CAs** is not yet on [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org). If you want to work with this GitHub version, you can install the latest status of the package from this repository with:

```{r install_option, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
if (!require(devtools)) install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("ugroempi/CAs")
```

or obtain a specific frozen status via a tag (so far the only tag is `v0.21` for version 0.21):

```{r install_option_tagged, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
devtools::install_github("ugroempi/CAs", ref="v0.21")
```

## Details
*At the end of this README file, charts depict the current status of array implementation relative to the empirical covering array numbers (eCANs) of the Colbourn tables, for v up to 10.*

```{r details, results = "asis"}
temp <- rd_html_get(rd_html, "Details", "Exported objects") 

# change equations back to $ for eqn and $$ for deqn
#   Find <code class=\"reqn\"> and then the very next </code>

start_token <- '<code class="reqn">'
end_token <- '</code>'
deqn_start_token <- '<p style="text-align: center;"><code class="reqn">'
p_token <- '<p>'
p_end_token <- '</p>'
p_align_token <- '<p style="text-align: center;">'

ind_start <- grep(start_token, temp)
ind_deqn_start <- grep(deqn_start_token, temp)

for (i in 1:length(temp))
{
  ## /deqn
  if (i %in% ind_deqn_start)
  {
    temp[i] <- gsub(start_token, "\n$$", temp[i])
    if (!grepl(end_token, temp[i]))
      stop("closing </code> tag is not on the same line as the start for an equation")
    temp[i] <- gsub(end_token, "$$\n", temp[i])
  }
  ## /eqn
  if (i %in% setdiff(ind_start, ind_deqn_start))
  {
    temp[i] <- gsub(start_token, "$", temp[i])
    if (!grepl(end_token, temp[i]))
      stop("closing </code> tag is not on the same line as the start for an equation")
    temp[i] <- gsub(end_token, "$", temp[i])
  }
}

## <p> tags
temp <- gsub(p_token, "\n", temp)
temp <- gsub(p_end_token, "\n", temp)
temp <- gsub(p_align_token, "\n", temp)

cat(temp)
```

## Current status of package implementation (for uniform CAs only)

The figures show performance percentages relative to the best-known arrays as collated by Colbourn, status November 2024; there are figures for up to 10&nbsp;levels and figures for up to 25&nbsp;levels; the reference scenarii are created as the union of situations for which NIST (2008) has arrays ($t=2,\dots,6$, $v=2,\dots,6$ but not both 6, with $k$ up to 2000 for $t=2$ and $t=3$ with $v$ up to 4, and decreasing maximum $k$ for larger $t$ and $v$) &minus;&nbsp;these have an array for each individual $k$ &minus; and the Colbourn table entries for $t=2,\dots,6$, $v=2,\dots,25$ and $k$ only where the necessary $N$ increases for the scenario; these are limited to situations with $N\le1.000.000$. This choice was based on convenience and could certainly be improved. For large $v$ (far outside of the NIST domain), the relative performance improves versus medium $v$; this is presumably due to a worse status of best-known arrays, not to a better status of implementation in the package.

```{r status1, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5}
## status_dat.rda was created by function status in file C:/rtests/CAsbak/inspectNs.R
bpFun <- function(ratiolim, vmax=10){
  load("C:/rtests/CAsbak/status_dat_0.22.rda")
  CAsVersion <- 0.22  ## !!! intentionally not automatic, because the status info 
                      ## !!! update is sometimes delayed versus the package update
  hilf <- status_dat[which(status_dat$v<=vmax & status_dat$N<=1000000),]
  par(mfrow=c(2,3), oma=c(0,0,3,0), mar=c(3.1, 3.1, 2.1, 1.1), cex=1.2, cex.main=1.2)
  for (t in 2:6){
    tab <- table(v=hilf[hilf$t==t,]$v,
          solution=((hilf[hilf$t==t,]$currentbestN/hilf[hilf$t==t,]$N) <= ratiolim))
    if (ncol(tab)==1) tab <- as.table(cbind('FALSE'=0, tab))
    bpt <- barplot(100*prop.table(tab,1)[,2],
          col=ifelse(sapply(2:25, function(obj) obj %in% CAs:::primedat$q), "steelblue3", "lightsteelblue1"),
          horiz=TRUE, las=1, plot=FALSE)
    prepplot::prepplot(c(0,100), c(0,vmax+1), gridx=TRUE, las=1,
        main=paste0("t = ", t), ylab="v", mgpx=c(1.5,0.05,0), 
          yticks=bpt[1:(vmax-1)], yticklabs=2:vmax)
    barplot(100*prop.table(tab,1)[,2],
          col=ifelse(sapply(2:25, function(obj) obj %in% CAs:::primedat$q), "steelblue3", "lightsteelblue1"),
          horiz=TRUE, add=TRUE, las=1, axes=FALSE, axisnames=FALSE, ann=FALSE)
    }
  prepplot::prepplot(c(0,1), c(0,1), axes=FALSE)
  legend(-0.1, 1, legend=c("v prime power", "other v"), fill=c("steelblue3", "lightsteelblue1"),
         bty = "n", xpd=NA)
  mtext(side=3, line=1, font = 2, cex=1.5, text=paste0("Percentage of strength t ", 
  ifelse(ratiolim<10, paste0("CAs with N at most ",
                                    100*ratiolim, " % of eCAN"), 
                      "scenarii for which there is any solution")),
        outer=TRUE)
  mtext(side=1, line=-1, font = 1, cex=1, text=paste0("Package version: ", CAsVersion), outer=TRUE)
  box(which="outer")
}

bpFun(Inf)
bpFun(1.25)
bpFun(1.05)
bpFun(1)

bpFun(Inf,25)
bpFun(1.25,25)
bpFun(1.05,25)
bpFun(1,25)

```


## References

**The Colbourn Covering array tables are currently unavailable at their usual location; temporarily, access is provided** [here](https://github.com/ugroempi/CAs/blob/main/ColbournTables.md).

```{r references, results = "asis"}
temp <- rd_html_get(rd_html, "References", "See") 
for (i in seq_along(temp))
{
  if (grepl("[\\]+Sexpr[[]results=rd,stage=build[]][{].+[}]", temp[i]))
  {
    m <- regexpr("[\\]+Sexpr[[]results=rd,stage=build[]][{].+[}]", temp[i])
    text1 <- substring(temp[i], 1, m-1)
    code <- substring(temp[i], m, m + attr(m, "match.length"))
    if (m + attr(m, "match.length") >= nchar(temp[i]))
    {
      text2 <- ""
    } else
    {
      text2 <- substring(temp[i], m + attr(m,"match.length") + 1, nchar(temp[i]))
    }
    code <- gsub(".*[{]", "", code)
    code <- gsub("[}].*", "", code)
    code <- gsub("tools:::Rd_expr_doi", "my_Rd_expr_doi", code)
    temp[i] <- paste(text1, eval(parse(text=code)), text2)
  }
}

# this is a fix for Issue 19 - https://github.com/bertcarnell/SOAs/issues/19

posit_found <- gregexpr("[_]II", temp[line_found])
```
